questions.question: For the model intramolecular Michael addition of nitroolefin 7, what result did Jacobsen's thiourea catalyst 9f give?

options.A: 70% yield as a single diastereomer in 99% ee
options.B: 51% yield as a single diastereomer in 96% ee
options.C: 95% yield in >99% ee on >5 g scale

questions.rationale: Catalyst 9f gave the best model reaction result; the simplified catalyst 9e gave the 51%/96% outcome.
questions.evidence_quote: provided the desired bicyclic nitroalkane 18 in excellent yield (95%) and near-perfect enantio-and diastereoselectivity (>99% ee, single diastereomer, >5g scale).

questions.question: How did the authors' DFT analysis rationalize the observed enantioselectivity of the key C–C bond-forming step?

options.A: Among 16 transition structures, TS1 was favored by 3.0 kcal/mol over the next-lowest and predicted 99% ee
options.B: TS1 was favored by 0.3 kcal/mol and predicted 70% ee
options.C: A single transition structure was found, with no competing pathway
options.D: The lowest-energy pathway was an intermolecular proton transfer, predicting racemic product

questions.rationale: The conformational search found 16 candidate transition structures and an energy gap matching the measured selectivity.
questions.evidence_quote: TS1 emerged as the most energetically favorable transition structure by G ‡ = 3.0 kcal mol -1 compared to the secondlowest-energy transition structure, amounting to a computed 99% ee

questions.question: What mechanistic consequence did the authors infer from the pKa ordering of nitro and ester acceptors?

options.A: Thiourea deprotonation by an enolate is favorable, whereas deprotonation by a nitronate is unfavorable, changing the preferred protonation pathway
options.B: Nitronate deprotonation is favorable, so both acceptors undergo the same intramolecular protonation
options.C: The ester has lower pKa than nitro, forcing only intermolecular protonation
options.D: The pKa values imply the C–C Michael addition is reversible for both substrates

questions.rationale: They attribute a change in protonation mechanism to the relative pKa values of nitro, thiourea, and ester.
questions.evidence_quote: the deprotonation of the thiourea by the enolate is favorable, whereas the deprotonation by the nitronate is unfavorable

questions.question: Which step enabled scalable installation of the butenyl chain in the route to nitroolefin 17?

options.A: Michael addition of an organozinc–copper complex gave nitroalkane 14 in 90% yield on 17 g scale
options.B: A Wittig reaction gave nitroalkane 14 in 52% yield on 5 g scale
options.C: Selenoxide elimination gave the butenyl chain in 86% yield
options.D: Reductive amination gave nitroalkane 14 in 70% yield on 17 g scale

questions.rationale: The organozinc–copper Michael addition was reported as scalable and high-yielding.
questions.evidence_quote: Installation of the butenyl chain was achieved by Michael addition reaction of an organo-zinc-copper complex

questions.question: What were the key conditions and outcome for desymmetrization precursor 17E?

options.A: 20 mol% catalyst 9f plus 20 mol% benzoic acid gave bicyclic adduct 18 in 95% yield, >99% ee, as one diastereomer on >5 g scale
options.B: 10 mol% 9e without acid gave 70% yield and 96% ee on 1 g scale
options.C: 20 mol% 9f plus 10 mol% benzoic acid gave 51% yield and 99% ee
options.D: 20 mol% proline gave 95% yield at 3.8:1 dr

questions.rationale: The optimized cyclization conditions yielded the desired product at multigram scale with near-perfect selectivity.
questions.evidence_quote: treatment of 17E with 20 mol% catalyst 9f in the presence of 20 mol% benzoic acid provided the desired bicyclic nitroalkane 18 in excellent yield (95%)

questions.question: What was the overall step count and target of the completed enantioselective total synthesis?

options.C: 24 steps to madangamines A, C, and E

questions.rationale: The authors report completion of the target synthesis in 30 steps.
questions.evidence_quote: A 30-step enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E has been achieved.

questions.question: How was the Z-configured skipped diene 28 obtained after the initial macrocyclization plan failed?

options.A: Early elimination of tertiary alcohol 27 using SOCl2 and DTBMP gave 90% yield and 4.3:1 Z-selectivity
options.B: Late-stage Wittig olefination gave 71% yield and 3.8:1 Z-selectivity
options.C: Ring-closing metathesis of S8 gave 90% yield with exclusive E selectivity
options.D: Hydrogenation followed by oxidation gave 4.3:1 Z-selectivity

questions.rationale: The revised sequence eliminated alcohol 27 early to form the desired Z diene.
questions.evidence_quote: early elimination of tertiary alcohol 27, proceeded to give the desired Z-configured skipped diene 28 in excellent yield and good Z-selectivity (90%, 4.3:1)

questions.question: Why did ring-closing metathesis fail for the initially proposed precursor S8 to form macrocyclic E?

options.A: The terminal alkenes were spatially too far apart; changing the order to eliminate the tertiary alcohol first enabled a later RCM
options.B: The catalyst decomposed because S8 contained a nitro group
options.C: The reaction gave only E-diene because the alkene geometry was wrong
options.D: The substrate could not be prepared in enantiopure form

questions.rationale: The authors attribute failed cyclization to alkene spacing and then changed the sequence.
questions.evidence_quote: All attempts to form the macrocyclic E ring via RCM resulted in no desired cyclisationa result attributed to the distant spatial arrangement of the terminal alkenes.

questions.question: What yield range did the authors report for installing the butenyl chain onto ketone 3 using Ishihara's triorganozincates?
questions.rationale: The triorganozincate reaction gave tertiary alcohol 27 in this yield range and reproducibly.
questions.evidence_quote: tertiary alcohol 27 could be afforded in high yields (70-78%)

questions.question: How many stereogenic centers did the key desymmetrization establish, and what feature did the DFT model invoke to explain selectivity?

options.A: Three, including a quaternary center; the favored transition structure benefits from multiple hydrogen bonds
options.B: Two, neither quaternary; selectivity arises from steric repulsion alone
options.C: Four, including two quaternary centers; the product is set by reversible proton transfer
options.D: One, with selectivity controlled only by solvent polarity

questions.rationale: The key irreversible Michael step sets all three centers, and the favored transition structure is stabilized by several H-bond interactions.
questions.evidence_quote: Both the relative and absolute stereochemical conﬁguration of the three newly formed stereogenic centers are set by the irreversible intramolecular Michael addition
